analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing
key_insights: Sales commentary dated Nov 16, 2026 (not research). US stocks closed lower: SPX -1.9%, NDX -2.7%, RTY -1.7%. 9 of 11 SPX sectors fell, with resilience limited to defensives.
Equal-weight held up better than the index: RSP -1% vs SPY -1.9%. Mag 7 fell 2.9% (NVDA -4.1%, GOOG -3.8%, TSLA -2.7%, AMZN -3.3%, META -2.4%).
AI trade fell again: semis -5.5%, hardware -4.7%, AI Data Centers & Power -3.5%. Software outperformed semis by 4.3%.

NVDA headlines are the main overhang. Huang's ouster raises doubts about Nvidia's support for neoclouds and the wider pool of AI funding. The US also moved to limit remote access to advanced AI chips.
Factor moves: Cyclicals vs Defensives -4.6%, Value L/S +2.6%, Recession L/S +2.0%, PURE Quality +1.6%.
Treasuries were mixed. The 5-year led gains (5y -2.0bp, 2y -1.0bp, 10y -0.4bp to 5.13%, 30y +0.9bp), reversing part of last week's CPI-driven rise in front and intermediate yields. DXY +0.2%.
Fed's Warsh said staff are gaming out contingencies on AI but did not discuss policy. Hammack said inflation is moving the wrong way.
Commodities fell: WTI -3.6% to $85.36, silver -3.6%, copper -1.4%, gold -0.8%.

Europe was a relative outperformer on the ex-AI rotation. SXXP had its best week in more than four months and an all-time high last Thursday. EU Defence and Luxury led, Healthcare outperformed with NOVO +2.4% on CagriSema data and an EU approval.
Eurozone industrial production printed +0.2% vs +0.3% survey. ECB's Vujcic backed market pricing for a 2027 hike. European yields were 1-4bp higher across the curve.
US floated a Donbas-for-NATO idea ahead of Thursday's Trump/Xi/Putin meeting.

Desk view: the sell-off came from weakness spreading beyond tech rather than one new catalyst. Investors are focused on the sustainability of AI financing and the capex cycle. NVDA earnings Tuesday night are the key test.

Retail Sales preview (Feroli, Nov 17): October headline flat MoM vs +0.1% survey and +0.8% prior. Gasoline station sales slow to +0.5% from +6.4%, vehicle dealer sales fall 1.1% on a 2.7% decline in unit auto sales. Control group expected +0.2%, food services +0.4%.

ETF flows (Rogerson): equity funds took in +$75bn last week. QQQ took +$11.3bn, ARKK +$5bn, CNEQ +$2.4bn, THRO +$3.2bn, CORO +$3.1bn. The desk was a real-money seller of SOXX/SMH, the first real position reduction seen there in its real-money client base.

Tech flow (Heavey): de-risking ahead of NVDA earnings. Money is rotating out of AI sectors, Info Tech is the largest sell sector, and Healthcare and Comm Services are the largest buy sectors. Volumes are 7% below the 5-day average. Neocloud names CRWV and NBIS show short pressing and memory is being sold long. SemiAnalysis cut out-year HBM and power estimates on slowing data center build momentum.
Heavey found the hyperscaler pullback surprising, since they stand to benefit most. META reversed Friday's gain after its LO meeting. SPCX was weak despite the Starship recapture.

NVDA sentiment (Meyers): frustration with Huang's behavior, and many expect more negative headlines. Petitions to bring him back exist, and some see an ambush by vested interests. Succession is unclear (Rene Haas and Lip Bu Tan are named). Circular financing is unlikely to continue at the same rate under a new CEO. Some see a China-hawk push to end exports to China, which would hurt open-source models and possibly NVDA. Some see NVDA's grip on the supply chain waning, which would help competitors and HBM prices.

Consumer desk (Barton): HD expected at a 2-handle on comps (buyside 2.0-2.5% vs Street +1.7%) with guidance reiterated. Positioning has shifted more long. Lower rates are needed for a durable big-ticket recovery.

NKE Analyst Day (Tuesday, webcast 11:30am ET): expected to guide FY28 revenue down YoY again, then LSD-MSD% growth, with a 10% 2031 operating margin target. Sentiment is negative, NKE is one of the most crowded fundamental shorts in Consumer, and the stock is near $40 at about 25x. Boss is bearish and has FY28 revenue at -2.8% vs Street about flat, with 2H implied guide at -7% at the midpoint.
Desk also cites AS slight beat expected (Tech Apparel mid-20s%, Outdoor high-20s%) and VIK net yields for Q3/Q4/FY27 of 2.1%, 2.3%, 4.2%.

US Market Intel view is Tactically Bullish. Positioning is cleaner and entry points more attractive. Inflation is the main risk but more an early-2027 problem, since a 50bp Fed hike in December is seen as highly unlikely.

Monetization Menu (Nov 16): the Anti-AI / ex-Tech rotation has dominated 2H26. The desk favors a move back to Tech with primary Mag7 exposure and options for an AI rebound, prefers Cyclicals over Defensives, and likes Europe for Cyclical/Value exposure, though a USD surge could temper it. SPX earnings track nominal GDP, so higher inflation is not bad for earnings.

Prior Monetization Menu (Nov 11, Dubravko's view): Tech washout at or near completion with some risk of another semis decline. Favors broad Tech plus options on US Memory and Semis, and a Tech plus Cyclicals barbell with Cyclicals played through Europe.
